skill.name: suggesting-tooling
skill.description: Analyzes a repository to recommend project-specific Claude Code skills and subagents. It matches detected languages, frameworks, workflows, and gaps to reusable tooling templates.
skill.summary: Recommend focused Claude Code skills and subagents from real codebase signals.
skill.author: BrendanShields

security_audit.summary: All 21 static findings are false positives after context review. The shell indicators are markdown fences or read-only local discovery examples, and the .env mention is a pattern signal rather than secret access. No prompt injection or malicious semantic intent was found.

remediation.issue: Markdown shell examples can trigger scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label discovery commands as optional, read-only checks and keep command arguments hardcoded.

remediation.issue: Secret-pattern wording is easy to misread.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that the skill detects secret-management signals without opening or displaying secret values.

content.value_statement: Teams often miss simple automation opportunities inside active codebases. This skill scans project signals and recommends focused Claude Code skills or subagents.
actual_capabilities: Detects primary languages from common source file extensions.
Identifies framework, test, workflow, and CI signals from common project files.
Maps detected signals to skill and subagent templates.
Ranks suggestions by impact using P1, P2, and P3 priority rules.
Checks existing .claude skills and agents to avoid duplicate tooling.
Prepares context prompts for approved skill or agent generation.
limitations: It relies on visible repository files and may miss behavior outside the workspace.
It provides recommendations and templates, not finished tooling unless another generator is used.
It needs user approval before generating new skills or agents.
It can over-suggest when project signals are sparse or ambiguous.

use_cases.title: Find Missing Workflow Helpers
use_cases.description: Review a repository and identify skills that would help repeated testing, documentation, or deployment tasks.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI Tooling
use_cases.description: Compare existing project workflows with current .claude tooling and prioritize shared recommendations for the team.

use_cases.title: Identify Delivery Automation Gaps
use_cases.description: Use CI, container, and deployment signals to decide which automation helpers would reduce manual release work.

prompt_templates.title: Find Tooling Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository and suggest Claude Code skills or subagents that would improve my daily workflow. Explain the evidence for each suggestion.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Recommendations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the detected languages, frameworks, CI files, and existing .claude tooling. Return at most five recommendations ranked by impact and duplication risk.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Generation Context
prompt_templates.prompt: For each approved recommendation, create concise context for a skill or subagent generator. Include purpose, detected signals, suggested tools, and expected limits.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Tooling Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare current .claude skills and agents against repository workflows. Identify overlaps, missing coverage, and which recommendations should become project standards.

output_examples.input: Suggest tooling for a TypeScript project with Jest tests and no existing skills.
output_examples.output: Recommended skill: testing-code. Evidence: Jest config and test files are present. Priority: P1 because tests exist without a project testing helper.

output_examples.input: Review a service with authentication middleware and token handling.
output_examples.output: Recommended agent: security-review. Evidence: authentication middleware and token handling appear in the repository. Priority: P1 for focused review workflows.

output_examples.input: Check whether a new linting skill is needed.
output_examples.output: Recommendation skipped: linting-code. Existing .claude tooling already covers linting, so a new skill would duplicate current workflow.

best_practices: Run the analysis from the repository root so project signals are complete.
Ask for evidence for each recommendation before approving new tooling.
Review generated skills and agents before adding them to a shared repository.
anti_patterns: Generating tools before confirming that the workflow is repetitive.
Suggesting agents for simple tasks that a short skill can handle.
Creating duplicate tools when existing .claude configuration already covers the need.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It reviews visible repository structure, common config files, workflows, and existing .claude tooling.

faq.question: Does it create skills automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends tooling first. Creation should happen only after explicit user approval.

faq.question: Can it work with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is useful for Codex and Claude Code when adapting AI tooling workflows.

faq.question: Does it read secret values?
faq.answer: It should detect only the presence of secret-management patterns. It should not read or expose secret values.

faq.question: How many recommendations should I expect?
faq.answer: The skill limits recommendations to focused, evidence-based suggestions, with at most five per category.

faq.question: When should I use a subagent instead of a skill?
faq.answer: Use a subagent for multi-step work that requires judgment. Use a skill for predictable, repeated tasks.
